about.baseTitle: A Pokhara base, not a Kathmandu desk
about.baseBody: We live by Phewa Lake. Permits, porters, and rest days start here — not from a catalogue in another city. When weather shifts a trail, the people who walk it are in the same town as you.
about.guidesTitle: Guides who know these paths by season
about.guidesBody: The same small team leads ABC, the Circuit, Poon Hill, Mardi, Dhampus, and Khopra. They pace for lungs, not for a clock. Rafting days use licensed river guides on the Kaligandaki.
about.licensesBody: Treks run with Annapurna Conservation Area permits and TIMS as required. Rafting follows Nepal river-safety rules and age limits we list on each trip. We will not pretend a monsoon week is a clear week.
about.localBody: Money stays in Pokhara: lodges, porters, drivers, river crews. You talk to a manager, not a call centre. There is no customer login because a trek is a conversation, not a dashboard.

plan.title: Plan the season before you pack.
plan.lede: October–November and March–April are the classic trek windows. Rivers run fuller in spring and after the monsoon. We will not sell you a view that cloud will hide.
plan.whoLede: Short days and big views, or a high pass with time to acclimatise. Read the trip, then send dates.
plan.riverLede: A Kaligandaki 1-day is the natural rest after a trek. Two- and three-day gorge trips are for guests who came for whitewater first.
plan.activityLede: Balloon mornings, zip and trolley thrills, three Pokhara-area bungees, and canyon swing — day experiences from Lakeside.
plan.safariLede: Chitwan for the classic Terai, Bardia for quieter tiger country, Dhorpatan for high-hill meadows — packages after the trek or alone.
plan.groupBody: Join a departure we are already running, or let us match dates with other walkers. Lower cost, shared pacing, tea-house rooms as they come.
plan.privateBody: Your dates, your speed, your group only. Tick the box on the booking form; a manager quotes the higher rate. It is not an online checkout.

prepare.title: Permits, packing, lungs, rivers.
prepare.lede: We handle ACAP and TIMS on the ground. You bring honest fitness, layers, and a passport that still has months on it.
prepare.permitsBody: Annapurna treks need an ACAP permit and usually a TIMS card. We organise them in Pokhara with your passport details. Costs sit in the quote, not as a surprise at the trailhead. Rafting does not use ACAP; river trips follow separate safety paperwork.
prepare.packingBody: Broken-in boots, a down layer, rain shell, sun hat, and a refillable bottle. Tea-houses sell snacks; they do not sell a spare knee. We send a season-specific list after you request dates. For rafting: swimwear, a dry change, and shoes that can get wet. We supply helmet, PFD, and paddle.
prepare.fitnessBody: Poon Hill is a steep holiday. ABC is a week of stairs. The Circuit asks for consecutive days and a high pass. Train on hills with a pack. We pace conservatively and will not push a sick guest over Thorong. Tell us about knees, asthma, and recent altitude before we lock a plan.
prepare.riverBody: Kaligandaki days are Grade III–IV and suit confident swimmers from the minimum age on the trip page. Everyone wears a helmet and PFD. We will refuse a run if the river is in flood. If you cannot swim, say so — we decide on the bank, not on a form.
prepare.ctaBody: Send dates. We reply with permits, pacing, and whether a Kaligandaki day fits after the trek.

footer.blurb: Locally owned trekking and rafting from the lake into the Annapurna Himalaya.

legal.privacyBody: We collect only what a booking needs: your name, email, phone, nationality, dates, and group size. We do not create customer accounts or sell your details. Staff in Pokhara use this information to confirm your trip and to reach you on the channel you prefer. You can ask us to delete a request by writing to the company email.
legal.termsBody: A submitted request is not a confirmed departure until a manager writes back with dates, price, and permit notes. Weather, ACAP and TIMS rules, trail and river conditions can change a plan. Cancellation and refund terms are confirmed in writing with your quote. Trekking and rafting in Nepal carry inherent risk; we brief honestly and pace conservatively.
